Logical replication is a method of replicating data objects and their changes, based upon their replication identity (usually a primary key). We use the term logical in contrast to physical replication, which uses exact block addresses and byte-by-byte replication. PostgreSQL supports both mechanisms concurrently, see Chapter 26. The walsender process starts logical decoding (described in Chapter 47) of the WAL and loads the standard logical decoding output plugin (pgoutput).
